Moengage._comment: Bangalore site (its clients.city is NULL — see scripts/backfill_client_city.sql). Mutton once a month is wired as a CAP now that a client menu import brought `dhaba_style_mutton_curry` into Bangalore; it was inert while the city carried no mutton at all. Cap rather than target for the same reason as Stripe's: with one eligible dish, a positive cadence would force that dish monthly regardless of the rest of the plate.

rules._comment: Banned in the main course: pumpkin, brinjal, yam and bisi bele bath. ingredient_ban matches key_ingredient AND primary_protein; the bath is a named dish, so it is banned by name in the rice slot.
rules.name: moengage_banned_ingredients

rules._comment: Mutton at most once a MONTH, enforced across plans from saved history (30-day window, the same shape as Pune's monthly oil-based bread). Selects on primary_protein — there is no is_mutton flag, and `dhaba_style_mutton_curry` is the Bangalore list's only mutton dish. Pairs with moengage_mutton_max_1 for the within-plan half.
rules.name: moengage_mutton_30d_window

rules._comment: The within-plan half: the history window only reads saved plans, so a single long horizon could otherwise place mutton on two of its own days.
rules.name: moengage_mutton_max_1

rules._comment: Bisi bele bath by name — it is a dish, not an ingredient.
rules.name: moengage_no_bisibele_bath

rules._comment: 'Week 1-2 egg non veg main is compulsory' — an egg dish in the non-veg slot on one or two days of the week, and compulsory, so it is a floor as well as a cap. `min: 1` is what makes it compulsory; `max: 2` is the upper end of the client's range. Bangalore carries 121 egg dishes in `nonveg_main`, so neither bound is at risk of relaxing. Counted in DAYS: this counter serves two non-veg dishes, so the one or two days it lands on may each carry an egg dish beside a chicken one — which is what a non-veg station does, and what `daily_max` would have to be added to prevent.
rules.name: moengage_egg_1_or_2_days
